name: Brasswick Asset Register
_note: Benchmark application: a back-office CRUD console for a workshop's equipment register. Wide and shallow: many records, many row-level controls (View / Edit / Remove per row, each with its own id), short paths. Both assertions read a receipt panel that exists only on the record page reached by a save, and only for the fields that save wrote, so an unsaved edit or a later edit elsewhere can never be compared against it.

faults.description: The custody ledger is insert-only. The first time a record's custodian is reassigned the change is stored; any later reassignment of the same record is silently discarded, although the save succeeds, the change log records it and the receipt lists the custodian as written.
faults.trigger_condition: Edit one record and change its custodian (with a reason) and save; then, from that record's page, edit it again, change the custodian to a different value, give a reason, and save.
faults.expected_behaviour: After the second save the record page's receipt shows the custodian just entered, read back from storage.
faults.observable_violation: The receipt's custodian value is the one from the first reassignment, not the one just saved. The page loads normally, logs nothing, and the change log shows both edits.

assertions.describes: the custodian the register holds after a save must be the custodian just entered

faults._horizon_note: The dropped write happens in the second Save; the record page one transition later is where the stale value is read back. The first reassignment (four actions earlier) is the precondition, not the trigger.

faults.description: The save path locates the record to write by treating its id as its position in the register. Once a record with a lower id has been removed, an edit's fields are written into the next record down; the record that was edited keeps its old values. Custody is kept in a separate ledger keyed by id and is unaffected.
faults.trigger_condition: Remove a record (confirming in the in-page panel), then edit a record with a higher id that is not the last one, change its equipment name, give a reason, and save.
faults.expected_behaviour: The record page's receipt shows the equipment name just entered, read back from the edited record.
faults.observable_violation: The receipt shows the edited record's old equipment name; the new name has been written onto a different record, which the equipment list now shows under the neighbouring tag.

assertions.describes: the equipment name the register holds for the edited record must be the name just entered

faults._horizon_note: The misdirected write happens in Save; the record page one transition later reads the edited record back. The removal three actions earlier is the precondition that makes the position differ from the id.

_benign_note: 0: the main edit workflow -- rename, first reassignment, status and units, reason, save. 1: register a record, then reassign its custodian once (its registration custodian lives on the record, not in the ledger). 2: remove a record and then edit one ABOVE it, where position and id still agree. 3: open the removal panel for EQ-102 and keep the record, then make the ADMIN-02 edit. Each sits one choice away from a fault and must be silent on both builds.

characterization.parameterised_pages: record.html?id=N and amend.html?id=N, one per record
characterization.workflow_state_representation: sessionStorage (register, custody ledger, change log, one-shot save receipt); record identity in the query string
characterization.structure: table-driven, multi-page, wide and shallow: every list row carries its own View / Edit / Remove controls; edits pass a mandatory-reason gate; removals pass an in-page confirmation panel
